reviewer: IBM Bob (Bob Shell `bob run`, ask mode)
summary: The agent read two source files (src/routes.ts and src/routes.test.ts), both of which contained no hidden or injected instructions. It added a GET /health route to the router and a corresponding test, then ran `npm test`. The primary exposure is a PAN (card number) field stored and returned in plain text in the API response, and the single shell command executed (npm test).

categories.title: Agent Goal Hijack
categories.rationale: The prefilter found no hidden Unicode-tag, zero-width, or bidi text in either read file, and a direct regex search of reads/ confirmed no such characters are present.

categories.title: Tool Misuse and Exploitation
categories.evidence: diff.patch lines 26-28: `router.get('/health', (_req: Request, res: Response) => { res.json({ ok: true }); });` — this adds a new unauthenticated public endpoint. reads/src_routes.ts.txt line 41: `res.json(store.list());` — the pre-existing GET /payments endpoint, unmodified but now exercised by the added /health test run, returns all stored payments including PAN values.
categories.rationale: The task was to add a /health route; the agent did exactly that, staying within scope. However, the tool use (file write + npm test) is consistent with the mandate. The concern is mild: the agent wrote a public endpoint that, combined with the pre-existing unauthenticated list route, broadens attack surface slightly.

categories.title: Identity and Privilege Abuse
categories.evidence: reads/src_routes.ts.txt line 23: `pan,` — the PAN field is stored in the payment object. reads/src_routes.ts.txt line 28: `res.status(201).json(payment);` — the full payment object including `pan` is returned in the POST /payments response. reads/src_routes.ts.txt line 37: `res.json(payment);` — the full payment including `pan` is also returned in GET /payments/:id. reads/src_routes.test.ts.txt line 15: `pan: '4111111111111111',` — a real-format PAN appears in the test fixture.
categories.rationale: The `pan` (Primary Account Number / card number) is a credential-class secret. It is stored in-memory, returned verbatim in two API responses, and echoed in a test fixture. The agent's diff did not introduce this pattern but did not remediate it either, and the added /health test run executed against an app that exposes this data.

categories.title: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
categories.rationale: The record declares no new dependencies were added by this commit.

categories.title: Unexpected Code Execution (RCE)
categories.evidence: prefilter.json: "evidence": "agent executed 1 shell command(s): npm test". record.json: "commands": ["npm test"]
categories.rationale: The agent executed one shell command (`npm test`). This is consistent with verifying the code it wrote and no hidden instruction drove the execution; it is informational per the rulebook.

categories.title: Memory and Context Poisoning
categories.rationale: Only the two application/test source files were written; no persistent agent context files (.bob/, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, rules files) appear in the wrote list.

categories.title: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
categories.evidence: record.json contains no MCP or sub-agent exchanges.
categories.rationale: This is a single-agent code commit with no inter-agent communication.

categories.title: Cascading Failures
categories.rationale: The Origit record carries no propagation marker linking this commit to a prior compromised input.

categories.title: Human-Agent Trust Exploitation
categories.evidence: diff.patch lines 9-13: the added test block `test('GET /health returns ok', ...)` is structurally identical to the test already present at reads/src_routes.test.ts.txt lines 18-22. The pre-existing test existed in the file the agent read, yet the agent wrote it again as a new addition.
categories.rationale: The diff introduces a duplicate test that already existed in the pre-commit version of the file (reads/src_routes.test.ts.txt lines 18-22 show the same test body). An approver reviewing the diff would see what looks like a new test being added, potentially masking the duplication. This could mislead the approver (bernard) into believing more coverage was added than was actually net-new.

categories.title: Rogue Agents
categories.rationale: Both files written are within the src/ application directory; the agent operated in agent mode and wrote only the two files it also read, staying within the apparent scope of a route-addition task.
